headline: EXCLUSIVE: Production Cybercabs ship with enhanced FSD compute — >32GB RAM vs. consumer fleet's 32GB ceiling; likely AI4+ (64GB) or dual-AI4 config; gives Cybercab headroom to run next-gen neural networks (FSD v15+) without hardware retrofit; confirms Cybercab is hardware-differentiated from consumer Model 3/Y at launch; whether AI4+, dual-board, or early AI5 engineering sample, the extra memory directly enables larger autonomous driving models fleet-wide (notateslaapp, Jul 7–8, 2026)

Tesla app 4.58.5 adds live 'Self-Driving' blue indicator — app now shows real-time FSD active status beneath speed readout; works across HW3/HW4; vehicle requires firmware 2026.20.6.1 (at ~49% fleet rollout as of Jul 7); critical for robotaxi fleet owners to monitor vehicle autonomy state remotely; concurrent app 4.58.6 adds new FSD state APIs (requires vehicle 2026.26+) for programmatic fleet monitoring; direct infrastructure for Cybercab fleet management at scale (notateslaapp / Teslarati, Jul 7–8, 2026)

TSLA recovers to $418–$424 on July 8 (+1–2%) as stock breaks above resistance line — TradingView cites $450 as next technical target; multi-day winning streak ahead of July 22 Q2 earnings; Yahoo Finance confirms analyst expectations for revenue growth and EPS upside vs. Q1; market digesting record Q2 delivery beat (480K, +25% YoY) while awaiting margin confirmation from July 22 report (TradingView / Yahoo Finance, Jul 8, 2026)

Polymarket assigns 10.5% odds on Tesla CA robotaxi by Dec 31, 2026 — and just 13% odds on Optimus external release by year-end; 247wallst notes 'crowd calling [Tesla's] timeline aspirational'; despite Q1 gross margin recovery to 21.1% and FSD subs +51% YoY, operating expenses jumped 37% on AI R&D and CEO SBC; bear/bull debate sharpening into July 22 earnings (247wallst / Polymarket, Jul 8, 2026)

TSLA falls -4.02% on July 7 as broader tech selloff sweeps Magnificent 7 — S&P 500 -0.45%, Nasdaq Composite -1.16% dragged by chip stock concerns and KOSPI (-4.9%) contagion after South Korea's market plunged; SpaceX (SPCX) fell 5% on its fast-track addition to the Nasdaq-100 index (effective July 7), triggering index-rebalancing outflows across large-cap tech; TSLA closed at $402.90 after tagging a $419.55 intraday high, giving back all of Monday's Tesla-specific optimism from Moravy's Giga Texas announcement; market squarely focused on July 22 Q2 earnings as the definitive margin catalyst — forward P/E of 204x means TSLA trades as an AI/robotics company, not an automaker, and gross margin print is the single swing factor heading into Q3 (TheStreet / CNBC / Investopedia / StockAnalysis, Jul 7, 2026)

Optimus production ramp accelerating at Fremont: 100–150 units/week targeted in July, ~300/week in August, 1,000/week by September — a potential 10x scale in 60 days that would be the steepest humanoid robot production ramp in history; Moravy confirmed Fremont line uses modular architecture that adapts as hardware evolves without teardown, enabling faster iteration; ex-Tesla Optimus AI scientist unveiled European humanoid startup Uma Robotics (Electrek, Jul 7) citing talent density as maturation signal; Q2 earnings call Jul 22 is expected to provide the first official production rate confirmation; if trajectories hold, Optimus transitions from R&D program to genuine volume production in Q3 2026 (BigGo Finance / Electrek, Jul 7, 2026)

Tesla Miami Robotaxi goes LIVE for rider service — first driverless rides outside Texas completed July 5-6; Tesla officially announced 'service is now available in Miami' on X July 5; geofenced area covers West Miami, Doral, and Coral Gables including Miami International Airport (MIA); Model Y fleet operational with no driver or safety monitor; first public rider videos and walkaround footage circulating on social media; TechTimes notes Florida's tropical rain is the hardest test yet for camera-only FSD — operating in precipitation, high humidity, and complex multi-lane airport approach roads; confirms Miami is Tesla's first operational driverless city outside Texas (gurufocus / TipRanks / TechTimes, Jul 5–6, 2026)

Electrek: Cybercab — 100+ units in Giga Texas outbound lot but unsupervised fleet shrinking to ~14 vehicles — Tesla is mass-producing a steering-wheel-less Cybercab it cannot yet sell or drive itself at scale; production-before-autonomy tension crystallized; Austin unsupervised fleet slid from peak ~25 active vehicles to ~14 as safety validation lags manufacturing; FSD crash rate ~4x human urban baseline per NHTSA; Musk confirmed robotaxi 'not material until 2027'; NHTSA self-cert path eliminates 2,500-unit cap so production scaling is uncapped; commercial passenger service gated by FSD v15 (end-2026/early 2027); manufacturing S-curve executing ahead of software timeline (Electrek, Jul 6, 2026)
